name: Estonia
summary: EU citizens register their residence. Non-EU nationals can get a large-investor permit with EUR 1 million in an Estonian company or fund, a business permit with EUR 65,000 in a company you hold shares in, a startup visa, or a digital nomad D visa for remote workers earning about EUR 4,500 a month gross (sources conflict). There is no passive-income or retiree permit found.
naturalisation: Eight years of residence, the last five on a permanent basis, Estonian at B1, and an exam on the Constitution and Citizenship Act. Time on the digital nomad visa gives no residence credit.
dual_citizenship_note: Naturalised citizens generally must renounce their former citizenship (Citizenship Act); exceptions and ancestry claims not verified (secondary sources).

routes.name: EU/EEA free movement
routes.summary: EU citizens register their residence with the local government; no permit.
routes.requirements: Directive 2004/38/EC; registration for stays over 3 months; permanent residence after 5 years.

routes.name: Residence permit for large investors
routes.summary: Permit for investing at least EUR 1 million in an Estonian company or fund.
routes.requirements: Direct, permanent investment of at least EUR 1,000,000 in an Estonian company investing in the Estonian economy, or in a fund investing mainly in Estonian companies; the value must not fall except through market moves; income of six times the subsistence level (set in the State Budget Act); health insurance. Permit up to 5 years, then extendable for up to 10 years at a time. Decision within 90 days.
routes.physical_presence: No residence requirement stated on the page (a secondary source says none)
routes.processing_time: Decision within 90 days, card within 30 days after
routes.tax_note: Becoming an Estonian tax resident follows the 183-day / permanent home test.
routes.fees_note: State fee not on the PPA page retrieved.

routes.name: Residence permit for business (shareholder)
routes.summary: Permit for owning shares in an Estonian company and investing EUR 65,000 in its activities.
routes.requirements: At least EUR 65,000 invested in the company's activities in Estonia; income of six times the subsistence level; sole-proprietor and start-up categories exist (amounts not retrieved; one secondary guide says about EUR 16,000 for sole proprietors). Subject to the immigration quota.
routes.physical_presence: Live in Estonia and run the business
routes.fees_note: State fee not stated on the page.

routes.name: Startup visa / start-up entrepreneur permit
routes.summary: Residence for founders of innovative, scalable startups approved by the Startup Committee.
routes.requirements: Approval by the Startup Estonia evaluation committee; no fixed investment. Fees and duration conflict between sources.
routes.physical_presence: Live in Estonia while running the startup

sources.title: Your guide to navigating Estonia's startup visa program

routes.name: Digital nomad visa (D visa for remote work)
routes.summary: Long-stay visa up to one year for remote workers employed or self-employed outside Estonia.
routes.requirements: Reported gross income of EUR 4,500 a month over the previous six months, from foreign sources (EUR 54,000 a year); other sources give EUR 3,960 or EUR 3,504; health insurance, clean record. Up to one year, extendable (18 months in one source). Outside the immigration quota. No residence credit toward citizenship.
routes.physical_presence: Live in Estonia; stays of 183+ days make you tax resident

sources.title: Estonia digital nomad visa: income requirement and quota

routes.tax_note: Estonia taxes residents at a 22% flat rate on worldwide income (secondary source); a 2026 security tax change was mentioned but not checked.

routes.name: EU Blue Card (work)
routes.requirements: Salary threshold is tied to the average wage; one aggregator gives about EUR 37,152 a year for 2026 but unverified. Contract of at least 6 months and relevant qualification.

sources.title: Estonia Blue Card: requirements and benefits for skilled workers
